findings.claim: Upgrading section says only v1 Codex, Copilot and VS Code hooks call the global binary. v1 Gemini CLI and Kiro hooks, and the Gemini MCP entry, call it too, so they also fail after npm uninstall -g.
findings.evidence: cm-main configs/gemini-cli/settings.json:10 "command": "context-mode hook gemini-cli beforetool"; configs/kiro/agent.json:8 "context-mode hook kiro pretooluse"; configs/gemini-cli/mcp.json "command": "context-mode"; src/adapters/gemini-cli/hooks.ts:135. Same wrong list in ADR-0011:76.
findings.fix: List every v1 agent whose hooks or MCP entry call the bare `context-mode` bin (Codex, Copilot CLI, VS Code, Gemini, Kiro, and Qwen if its adapter does), taken from detectV1 per agent, not from memory.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY c56afc99 2026-03-05 'feat: global install + CLI hook dispatcher'. ORIGINAL_INTENT: 'All platforms now use `npm install -g context-mode` as prerequisite ... This ensures ctx-upgrade persists across sessions'. REGRESSION_RISK: Gemini/Kiro users uninstall npm and get hook errors with no warning. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: doc only; keep ADR-0011 order.

findings.claim: Privacy row says network use is limited to `git ls-remote` and the agent's git fetch. ctx_index fetches URLs, ctx_execute runs user code that can use the network, and ctx_upgrade fetches the release commit for git installs.
findings.evidence: docs/v2/prompt/drafts.md:34 'or a URL, which is fetched and converted to Markdown'; ADR-0010:44 'fetch the latest `release` commit into a new version dir'; TECH-SPEC:291 GP5 'proxy env'.
findings.fix: Say: context-mode itself makes network calls only when you ask (ctx_index on a URL, ctx_upgrade on git installs) plus `git ls-remote` in ctx_doctor; code run in ctx_execute has your normal network access. No telemetry, no LLM calls.

findings.claim: Install rule 'a row gets a command only after a live install test passes' does not say which test counts, who runs it, or where the pass is recorded. The keyless harness can only run claude and codex, so 8 of 10 rows have no path to a command, and ADR-0011 already prints untested Gemini/Qwen commands.
findings.evidence: ADR-0012:17 'only `claude` and `codex`. The others are not installed and print `SKIPPED`'; ADR-0011:42 Gemini/Qwen command with no test note vs :43-45 'test first'; TECH-SPEC:287 GP1 is a contract test, not a live install.
findings.fix: Define the gate: the test id (e.g. GP-LIVE-INSTALL per agent), the agent version, and a dated record file (e.g. metrics or e2e report) the README row links to. Mark the ADR-0011 Gemini/Qwen rows 'test first' until that record exists.

findings.claim: 'fail until /ctx-upgrade runs' assumes a v2 /ctx-upgrade command exists on Codex, Copilot CLI and VS Code. TECH-SPEC marks skill commands on those agents as unverified. Also a user who runs /ctx-upgrade before installing v2 gets the v1 command, which says 'Already on latest'.
findings.evidence: TECH-SPEC:210 'Whether each one exposes a skill as a `/` command ... **[U] S-SKILLS**'; ADR-0011:15 v1 /ctx-upgrade prints 'Already on latest' when main is frozen. v1 command added in d6efc67e 2026-03-05 'feat: universal ctx commands via MCP meta-tools'.
findings.fix: Write the step as: install v2 first, then run /ctx-upgrade or tell the agent 'call the ctx_upgrade tool'. Warn that v1 /ctx-upgrade will not move to v2.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY d6efc67e 2026-03-05 'feat: universal ctx commands via MCP meta-tools'. ORIGINAL_INTENT: one command name across agents. REGRESSION_RISK: users run the old command, see 'Already on latest', and stay on v1 with broken hooks. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: keep main frozen (ADR-0011:15); doc wording only.

findings.claim: 'Steps in ADR-0011 order' points to the maintainer release order (version bump, marketplace ref, docs, npm deprecate), not to user steps. The user steps are the per-agent table in ADR-0011 step c.
findings.evidence: ADR-0011:28-54 steps a-d are owner actions; user commands are the table at ADR-0011:38-46.
findings.fix: Say: user steps per agent = ADR-0011 step c table, in this order: install v2, run ctx_upgrade to remove v1 leftovers, then npm uninstall -g, then restart.

findings.claim: Target length is 'about 165 lines', but the section budgets sum to 129 lines.
findings.fix: Set the target to the sum (about 130) or add the missing 35 lines to named sections.

findings.claim: 'CI cap of 200' lines has no CI job or GS gate that enforces it.
findings.evidence: grep -i 'readme|lines' in TECH-SPEC.md GS1-GS7, adr/0013-release-automation.md and .claude/skills/release/SKILL.md: no README length check.
findings.fix: Add a check (e.g. in GS5 or the release skill pre-flight) that fails when README.md exceeds 200 lines, and that `## Install` exists (npm deprecate link target).

findings.claim: Clones badge reads `metrics/traffic.json`, written weekly by a cron job. Scheduled workflows run on the default branch (main), which is frozen, so the badge source either needs commits on main or a different branch that the doc does not name.
findings.evidence: ADR-0015:54 'Nothing changes on `main` without owner approval'; ADR-0011:80-88 traffic.yml cron with contents: write, 'commits only when the file changed', no branch named.
findings.fix: Name the branch traffic.yml writes to (e.g. a `metrics` branch) and point the badge URL at that branch.

findings.claim: Issues row targets humans only. Owner rule: issue flow must be aimed at AI agents and get maximum debug data. The README is what an agent reads first, but row 11 does not tell the agent to call ctx_doctor and paste the full report unchanged.
findings.evidence: ADR-0015:22 'issues need the `/ctx-doctor` report'; ADR-0014:57 bug.yml text 'tell the agent: call the ctx_doctor tool'. Owner rule (this run): 'issue template i tamamen ai agentlere yonelik olmali ... maksimum debug verisini gondermeli'.
findings.fix: Add one agent-directed line: 'AI agents filing an issue: call ctx_doctor, paste the whole ctx-report block byte for byte, and fill every field of bug.yml.'
